thread:
Dev Patel: Heads up — we’ve got a cluster of tickets this morning with the same theme: “status page says API operational but embeddings are failing.” Customers are screenshotting status.redwoodinference.com and calling us out.

Support Bot: New Jira issues created from Support triage: SUP-28411, SUP-28549

Rachel Kim: +1. I’m on SUP-28411 (Northbridge). They have 5xx spikes on `/v1/embeddings` in us-east ~30 mins, but Chat completions are fine. They’re saying our status page is “misleading” because the top-level API component stays green.

Jasmine Liu: Also got an escalation from Lattice. Similar story: embeddings timeouts + retries, but everything else stable. They’re asking for “component-level status” by capability. This is exactly what they flagged in procurement.

Dev Patel: Can we please split embeddings out as its own public component? Right now the “Hosted API” umbrella hides partial outages and Support gets stuck arguing semantics.

Owen Phillips: What are you telling them right now? We need a consistent macro. We can’t say “status page wrong” but we also shouldn’t gaslight.

Rachel Kim: Current response I’m using (paraphrasing): we’re investigating reports of elevated errors on embeddings in us-east; internal metrics indicate partial impact; status page will be updated if thresholds are met. But customers are like “why not just mark it now.”

Dev Patel: Exactly. Even if the platform is broadly fine, embeddings being down is a big deal for folks. We’re getting ticket churn.

Rafael Mendes: Jumping in — yes, we’re tracking this. The component taxonomy work is in flight. Today the status page is too coarse (Hosted API + a few regions), and partial capability outages don’t always trip the right public component.

Rafael Mendes: For this specific pattern: embeddings errors can be masked if overall gateway error % stays below the Hosted API threshold. We need capability-level components (Embeddings, Reranking, Streaming, Chat/Generate) at least per “key regions.”

Christine Wong: +1. We have a draft component registry that splits “Hosted API” into capabilities. Embeddings is explicitly called out because of tickets like these.

Christine Wong: Question for Support: do customers care more about per-region or per-capability? (we can do both, but it’ll expand the component list and increase comms overhead).

Jasmine Liu: From CS side: both. The most common phrasing we get is “embeddings in us-east” or “streaming in eu-west” — they want to know if it’s their region + the specific feature.

Rachel Kim: Agree. If we had just “Embeddings” globally it’s still better than today, but it would also cause confusion when only one region is impacted.

Allison Grant: Observability note: we can support per-capability + per-region as long as we standardize the signal source and anti-flap rules. Otherwise the status page will oscillate and on-call will hate us.

Dev Patel: From Support POV: I’d rather have a slightly longer component list than keep dealing with “status page says all good” when one capability is on fire.

Owen Phillips: Can we get a stopgap? Like a guideline for when Support can request a manual status update even if the aggregate component doesn’t trip.

Rafael Mendes: Yes. We’re updating the incident comms process to include a Comms Lead + earlier “Investigating” updates with clear scope (“Embeddings in us-east”). For now, if you see ≥3 independent customer reports + you can point to a dashboard panel, page #incidents and ask IC to consider a component-level update.

Rachel Kim: What should we tell the customers in the meantime? Specifically, they’re asking “why didn’t the status page reflect this.”

Christine Wong: Suggested wording (safe): “Our status page currently groups multiple API capabilities together, which can under-represent partial impact. We’re actively improving component granularity so incidents affecting specific capabilities/regions are reflected more precisely.”

Jasmine Liu: That’s good. Please avoid anything that sounds like we’re admitting we hid an incident.

Dev Patel: :thumbsup: Can we turn that into a macro and link to the upcoming post-incident summaries format? Customers keep asking for a consistent writeup.

Owen Phillips: I’ll open an internal ticket to update the support macros once we have final approved language.

Allison Grant: Also worth noting: we found at least one misclassification issue in the component map previously (embeddings vs chat). Fix is in progress, but we should assume some of these “status mismatch” complaints are legit signal.

Rafael Mendes: Action items:
- Christine to confirm component split includes “Embeddings (Hosted) / us-east, eu-west, us-west” in the first public rollout
- Support to drop the macro language into SUP-28411 / SUP-28549 and tag me if they push back
- Allison to share the dashboard link you’re using so we can align thresholds

Rachel Kim: Thanks. I’ll reply to Northbridge with the macro language + note that we’re improving status page granularity. Will also include that we can share a post-incident summary when available.

Dev Patel: Appreciate it. Please keep us posted on the rollout timing — this is becoming a repeat escalations category.

Rafael Mendes: Will do. Target is staged rollout after taxonomy + mapping lands. We’ll announce internally first so Support isn’t surprised by new components.

Support Bot: Reminder: SUP-28411 is marked Priority: High. Next update due in 2h per Support SLA.
